$comment: Usage rules for each Figma text style. Values (size, weight, line height…) come from figma-variables.json; this file only says when to use what. Shown on the Typography page and published to public/tokens/typography.json and public/llms.txt by `npm run tokens`.
intro: Type tokens for body text and headings, organised around t-shirt sizes — large, medium, small — to make it easy to build multiple levels of hierarchy.
rules: Always set text with a .text-* class (or its CSS variables). Never hard-code font-size, font-weight, line-height or letter-spacing.
Use headings for hierarchy and body styles for content; don't use a heading style just to make text bigger.
Use the strong variant of a body style for emphasis within the same size, not a heading style.
Display is reserved for onboarding and heavily branded moments — at most one per view.
Pair type with semantic text color tokens (e.g. --color-text-default, --color-text-secondary), never primitives.

styles.label: Display
styles.usage: To create continuity with our logged-out marketing views, we sparingly use Inter for onboarding and other heavily branded moments.
styles.sample: Large display size for expressive moments and important announcements

styles.label: Large heading
styles.usage: Our largest heading size, reserved for elements like the primary page title within large views.

styles.label: Medium heading
styles.usage: Section headings within a page or large panel.

styles.label: Small heading
styles.usage: Headings for compact areas like cards, panels and grouped lists.

styles.label: Body Large
styles.usage: Our largest body text size, usually saved for elements like multiline text.

styles.label: Body Medium
styles.usage: Our default text size for the majority of UI elements in the editor, such as inputs and buttons.

styles.label: Body Small
styles.usage: Our smallest text size, primarily used by small UI elements like avatars and badges.
